messages:
maria_cs: FYI received a high-priority ticket — customer says codegen used to compile fine, after last rollout their CI is failing with compilation errors. They pasted the prompt + generated output. Can someone triage? 

aj_devx: Thanks — can you paste the exact prompt + a small repro? also which model tag/version did they hit?

maria_cs: here's the prompt snippet they used and the model header they hit: model: redwood-codegen-3.2.0 (rolled out ~3h ago)

```prompt
// Generate a TypeScript function that fetches user metadata and returns a typed User object
// Requirements: use fetch, handle non-200, return `User | null`
```

Customer's generated output (truncated):
```ts
async function getUser(id: string): Promise<User> {
  const res = await fetch(`/api/users/${id}`)
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error('fetch failed')
  const data = await res.json()
  // missing return statement and incorrect type usage
  const user = { id: data.id, name: data.name }
}
```

maria_cs: They point out the missing `return` and also we used to provide a `User | null` signature and a null branch. This used to compile in their CI with v3.1.8.

eli_research: interesting. That looks like an instruction-following regression — model dropped the final line. Could be a decoding/stop token or prompt formatting change. Any difference in system prompt or generation config between 3.1.8 and 3.2.0?

aj_devx: I checked infra logs — during rollout we changed default sampling from greedy to top-p=0.95 for a config experiment on code models. Might explain missing final lines if model truncates. I will run a quick diff.

sam_infra: deploy-bot indicates: "deploy-bot: canary deploy redwood-codegen-3.2.0 -> 10% traffic at 2025-11-03T14:12Z" --- that matches timeline.

aj_devx: quick A/B: I ran the same prompt against pinned v3.1.8 and v3.2.0 in sandbox: v3.1.8 output includes proper return and null branch; v3.2.0 result truncates before return 4/5 times at temp 0.0, and 2/5 at top-p 0.95 it truncates more.

eli_research: good repro. hypothesis: the generation length penalty or stop sequence changed; also we applied a tokenizer update for edge-case delimiters. I'll run the unit eval suite for codegen prompts and produce a diff of AST-level checks. Give me ~45m.

maria_cs: customer asked for a hotfix — they want their org pinned to last known good model until resolved. Org id: org_7Yx-zz. They also included CI logs complaining: TS2345 type mismatch because function signature differs.

sam_infra: I can add a routing override. Will create an emergency route to pin org_7Yx-zz -> redwood-codegen-3.1.8 and zero-downtime route change. ETA 10m.

sam_infra: done — routing override applied for org_7Yx-zz. :white_check_mark: 

maria_cs: shared the temporary routing update with the customer; they confirm CI started passing again. They want a postmortem and ETA to re-enable.

eli_research: preliminary eval shows a ~3.7% regression on our codegen compilation metric after the rollout when using the new decode defaults. I'll run with old decode settings on 3.2.0 to isolate model vs decode defaults.

aj_devx: if it's decode defaults, we can consider changing default config back for codegen families while keeping other perf changes. Also we should add a changelog note for default decoding changes.

ron_sales: Customer flagged this as blocking release for their product — asking for an internal update before EOD. Keep me in the loop.

eli_research: will post results to thread when complete. Tentative next steps: 1) keep org pinned 2) run blue/green test with decode settings from v3.1.8 on v3.2.0 3) if passes, push config rollback for codegen-only traffic 4) if fails, revert model rollout.

aj_devx: sounds good. Also adding an automated smoke test to CI that checks for missing returns/unfinished functions via a small AST linter on a held-out prompt set. :+1:

maria_cs: thanks team — I updated the customer and logged the escalation. Will open a support case for the postmortem notes. :eyes:
